applies_to: Belimo 6-way EPIV (EP..R-R6+BAC) used to switch and control a single coil between heating and cooling sequences.
summary: The 6-way EPIV combines a 6-way changeover valve with a flow sensor, so one coil can be fed from either a heating or a cooling circuit with flow control. On BACnet MS/TP a single AO 1 setpoint covers both sequences: in flow control, 0-33% runs sequence 1 from Vmax1 down to zero, 33-67% is the dead band, and 67-100% runs sequence 2 from zero up to Vmax2. It reports flow, position, active sequence and status.
notes: MV 100 ControlMode has no access marking in the document, so it is listed read-only here; it is likely writable.
MO 1 state 6 is printed with the same text as state 5.
MV 121 sets the unit of AI 19, AI 109 and AV 119 (the document refers to AV 119 as AI 119).
Air bubbles in the system force position control until they clear, regardless of MV 100.

integration.summary: Set MV 122 SpSource to Bus and command AO 1 SpRel, remembering that in flow control the 0-100% range is split into sequence 1, dead band and sequence 2. Set Vmax1 and Vmax2 once at commissioning. Read AI 19 flow, MI 1 active sequence and BI 101 summary status.

minimum_points.name: SpRel
minimum_points.why: Single setpoint for both heating/cooling sequences

minimum_points.name: SpSource
minimum_points.why: Must be Bus for AO 1 to take effect

integration.enable: Write MV 122 SpSource = 2 (Bus); with Analog (default) the valve follows the 0-10 V signal on wire 3. MO 1 Override can force sequence 1 or 2 open, close, or a sequence Vmax.
setup: MS/TP only: baud 9600-76800, default 38400; MAC address 0-127, default 10.
Max 32 nodes without repeater; the 120 Ω terminating resistor must be fitted externally.
gotchas: Writable objects with instance 90 and above are persistent; do not write them on a regular basis.
In flow control, setpoints 33-67% are a dead band with zero flow.
